subject: AtlasBank — stability reconciliation, timeline, and customer verification request
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial summary — what we saw and next steps (AtlasBank)

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the quick sync a short while ago. I wanted to follow up with a concise summary of what Redwood observed during the disruption on 2028-05-21 and the immediate actions we've taken.

Summary (high level):
- Impact window: ~2028-05-21 02:42:00 UTC to 2028-05-21 05:28:00 UTC. Intermittent request failures and elevated token latency for a subset of AtlasBank production traffic routed to eu-west-1.
- Root cause (initial): a scheduling race during a staged GPU kernel rollout caused a small percentage of serving instances to run a mismatched kernel compilation, which in turn produced session-affinity mismatches and KV-cache misses for active sessions.

Immediate actions taken by Redwood:
- We paused the rollout and rolled back the kernel set across the affected pool.
- Recovered affected instances and forced a controlled cache warm-up pass to rehydrate prefix/KV entries.
- Opened a dedicated verification window and increased tracing for AtlasBank routes; we preserved request traces and token-level timing for your review.

Attachments: we are including an annotated timeline, the engineering root-cause note, and a verification checklist.

Next steps we propose:
1) A short technical readout with your platform team — 30 minutes — to walk the timeline and confirm validation steps.
2) Access for AtlasBank to the collected traces and the verification checklist so you can sign off.
3) Our longer-term mitigation plan items (listed in the attached note).

Can you confirm availability for a brief readout tomorrow (Wed) 09:00–12:00 UTC or suggest another slot?

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasbank.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial summary — additional technical detail and mitigation

Sam / Tessa — adding a few technical details for the AtlasBank platform team ahead of the readout: please feel free to circulate to your infra owners.

What happened (technical):
- During an automated kernel rollout (aimed at a latency optimization), a small subset (approx. 3%) of the eu-west-1 serving pool accepted a kernel binary that had been staged but not fully validated for the active model config. That binary included a gating change in the KV serialization path.
- The mismatch did not crash inference processes but produced inconsistent KV-key serialization for ongoing sessions. That inconsistency caused session affinity logic to treat re-routed requests as cold (miss) and resulted in elevated token latency and a low rate of malformed session responses.
- The autoscaler reacted to latency and briefly added capacity; as new instances came up they inherited the same mismatched kernel until the rollout was stopped.

Why it was hard to detect early:
- Signal was noisy and affected only a narrow slice of route topology (prefix-dependent), so synthetic health checks did not surface it.

Short-term mitigations we performed:
- Immediate rollback of the staged kernel and forced a version pin for the pool.
- Targeted cache warm-up (controlled replay of recent prefixes) to rehydrate affected sessions.
- We created a temporary routing exclusion for the older session affinity paths while we verified correctness.

Permanent/near-term engineering changes we will implement:
- Add a kernel-compatibility gate that runs a small synthetic prefix verification before marking a kernel as generally available.
- Tighten autoscaler hysteresis for kernel-rollout windows to prevent capacity churn from amplifying edge cases.
- Expand tracing to include a short KV-serialization digest for post-rollout validation.

I'll present a succinct technical timeline in the readout; Tessa, we should include the timeline CSV and the annotated PDF.

-M

Attachment referenced: root-cause-note-20280525.pdf
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasbank.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2028 08:29:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Initial summary — availability and verification items

Tessa / Marissa — thanks for the quick follow-up and very clear write-up. We can confirm a 30-minute readout on Wed 22 May at 10:00 UTC. AtlasBank attendees: myself, Priya Anand (platform lead), and Diego (SRE).

A few asks from our side before the call:
- Please provide the preserved traces and a short guide to interpret the KV-serialization digest.
- Can you highlight whether any customer data was exposed or at risk (our security/compliance team needs an explicit statement)?
- We will want a timeline keyed to our request IDs — if you can map traces to the sample request ids in the CSV that will help our verification.

We'll review the attachments you sent and join the readout.

Sam
Senior Platform Manager
AtlasBank
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@atlasbank.com>, Priya Anand <priyaa@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Closure & verification steps — artifacts shared and remediation commitments

Hi Sam / Priya — thanks again for the readout earlier this week and for the constructive questions. Following up with the artifacts and the formal commitments we discussed.

Artifacts shared (links / attachments):
- Annotated timeline (atlassvc_timeline_20280521-25.csv) — maps to request IDs we pulled for your sample set.
- Root cause note (root-cause-note-20280525.pdf) — short engineering summary with the proposed remediation items.
- Verification checklist (verification-checklist.xlsx) — step-by-step guide your SRE team can run; includes expected artifact locations and pass/fail indicators.
- Traces: shared in the Drive link (retained traces are scrubbed for PII; schema and digest mapping included).

Security statement: no customer data was exfiltrated or exposed. The condition was an internal serialization inconsistency; we audited request/response payloads and confirmed no unexpected content appeared in logs outside of expected redacted tokens. Our security team has performed an independent review; summary included in the root-cause PDF.

Remediation commitments & timelines:
- Compatibility gate for staged kernels — implementation and rollout schedule: 3 weeks (ETA 2028-06-15).
- Autoscaler hysteresis adjustments — config change next week, monitored for 2 weeks.
- Expanded tracing (KV-serialization digest) — instrumentation in Canary within 10 days, full rollout over 4 weeks.

Acceptance ask: please run the verification checklist and confirm by responding to this thread once your SREs have completed the steps. If you hit any failing checks, flag them and we'll prioritize immediate remediation.

If you prefer, we can move the verification into a joint session where our engineers run the checklist with your team — happy to schedule.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
